newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to name panel on health care quality.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to name panel on health care quality.

text.p: President Clinton is set to name most of the members of his new commission on health care quality on Wednesday, administration sources said Tuesday.
Amid a rapidly changing health sector, the new panel will look at a variety of issues concerning health care quality and patient rights in managed care and traditional fee-for-service settings.
But it will not be charged with recommending an overall national health insurance plan, like the one Clinton tried and failed to enact in his first term.
Clinton announced his plans last September for the commission, which will be chaired by the secretaries of Health and Humans Services and Labour.

Noting that the health care system was undergoing rapid changes in its structure and financing, Clinton said when he made the announcement, "We have to make sure that the changes that are being made do not lead to a decline in the quality of health care."

Some Republicans said they fear the commission is the start of another liberal attempt to impose greater government regulation on health care. But health advocacy groups have generally welcomed the panel, and some of the bills introduced in Congress about health care quality and managed care have had bipartisan support.
